translationRepairs: Book of Sui, 77th year of Volume, 42th year of Biography
s0001 is 隋書卷七十七列傳第四十二: 卷七十七 and 列傳第四十二 are volume and biography numbers, not years. Volume 77, Biography 42 matches the Chinese and the existing literal.

Early in the Kaihuang reign, Prince Xia of Qin recommended him; he placed at the top of the policy examination and was ordered to join the Confucian scholars in fixing rites and music, receiving appointment as Collator.

Early in the Kaihuang reign, Prince Xiao of Qin recommended him; he placed at the top of the policy examination and was ordered to join the Confucian scholars in fixing rites and music, receiving appointment as Collator.
s0105 has 秦孝王; 孝 is Xiao (filial), so Prince Xiao of Qin is required. Xia misreads that character.
During the Taikang period of Chen he answered a summons and stayed for a time at the Zhizhen Abbey.
During the Taijian period of Chen he answered a summons and stayed for a time at the Zhizhen Abbey.
s0175 dates the episode to 陳太建時; 太建 is the Chen era Taijian, not Taikang. The proposed idiomatic fix restores the correct era name.
During the Taikang era of Chen, summoned, he came to rest at the Zhizhen Abbey.
During the Taijian era of Chen, summoned, he came to rest at the Zhizhen Abbey.
The literal likewise misrenders 太建 in 陳太建時 as Taikang; Taijian is the correct reading of that Chen era name.

Yet Shiqian, hearing praise, was not pleased; Wenbi, seeing injury, was not angry; Ze's aim lay in deep obscurity—none could draw him near or push him away, none could make him noble or base—all were men who embraced simplicity.

Yet Shiqian, hearing praise, was not pleased; Wenxu, seeing injury, was not angry; Ze's aim lay in deep obscurity—none could draw him near or push him away, none could make him noble or base—all were men who embraced simplicity.
s0253 names 文詡; 詡 is xǔ, so Wenxu is required. Wenbi is a wrong romanization of the same person.
